questions.question: If you drive a school bus during high winds, you should:

options.text: Loosen your grip on the steering wheel.

questions.explanation: Slow down when driving a school bus in high winds. Hold the steering wheel firmly and watch for wind gusts.

questions.question: When exiting your vehicle, you must keep ____ in contact with the vehicle at all times.
questions.explanation: When exiting your vehicle during the basic control skills test, face the vehicle and keep three points in contact at all times. On a bus, hold the handrail. Not doing this correctly will fail the test.

questions.question: When checking the fifth wheel gap during pre-trip inspection, you should:

options.text: Make sure the locking jaws are open.
Make sure the locking jaws are fully closed around the kingpin.
Make sure the locking jaws are loose.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the locking jaws are fully closed around the kingpin.
questions.explanation: The fifth wheel locking jaws must be closed around the kingpin shank, not the kingpin head.

questions.question: Outside mirrors should be adjusted:
questions.explanation: Check and adjust all mirrors on a school bus before you drive.

questions.question: During a basic vehicle control skills test, you may be asked to:

options.text: Drive straight into a parking space.

questions.explanation: The basic control skills test may include straight line backing, offset back/right parking, offset back/left parking, driver side parallel parking, conventional parallel parking, and alley docking.

questions.question: When should you check the mirrors on a bus?

options.text: You do not need to check the mirrors

questions.explanation: Check the mirrors on a bus before you drive. Adjust them as needed before you start.

questions.question: An outside convex mirror is properly adjusted if:

options.text: You can see at least one traffic lane and the entire side of the bus.
You can see the front bumper.
You can see the top of the bus.
You can see the front windshield.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can see at least one traffic lane and the entire side of the bus.
questions.explanation: The outside convex mirrors should show the front of the rear tires touching the ground, each side of the bus up to the mirror, and at least one traffic lane on each side.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test, you must be able to do all of the following, except:

options.text: Show where the power steering fluid dipstick is located.
Check that there is enough power steering fluid.
Make sure the power steering fluid is above the full mark.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the power steering fluid is above the full mark.
questions.explanation: During the pre-trip inspection, you will show where the power steering fluid dipstick or sight glass is. You will check that the fluid is at a safe level.

questions.question: During a basic vehicle control skills test, you may be asked to:

options.text: Pull forward into a parking space.

questions.explanation: The basic control skills test may include straight line backing, offset back/right parking, offset back/left parking, driver side parallel parking, conventional parallel parking, and alley docking.

questions.question: When boarding the school bus, students should:

options.text: Take two stairs at a time.

questions.explanation: Students should board a school bus slowly in a single-file line while using the handrail.

questions.question: Who can change school bus stops?
questions.explanation: Only the school district can change bus stop locations. The driver needs written permission from school officials to make any changes.

questions.question: What should the driver do when students board a school bus?
questions.explanation: The driver should watch all mirrors while students board. This helps catch any students running to catch the bus.

questions.question: What should a driver do if they need to leave the bus to check on a student?

options.text: Turn off the engine and take the key.
Ask another bus driver to watch the bus.
Ask all students to exit the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off the engine and take the key.
questions.explanation: Always secure the bus before leaving it. Turn off the engine and take the key. Then check around and under the bus for the missing student.

questions.question: What should the driver see in a properly adjusted outside mirror?

options.text: Where the front of each rear tire touches the ground.
Where the front of each front tire touches the ground.

questions.correctAnswerText: Where the front of each rear tire touches the ground.
questions.explanation: Outside mirrors should show one traffic lane on each side of the bus, the entire side of the bus, and where the front of each rear tire touches the ground.

questions.question: How far behind the bus should properly adjusted mirrors allow the driver to see?
questions.explanation: Properly adjusted mirrors let the driver see 200 feet behind the bus. This is about four bus lengths.

questions.question: How should a driver approach a school bus stop?
questions.explanation: Always approach bus stops slowly and carefully.

questions.question: What should the driver do if a student is missing after exiting the bus?

options.text: Secure the bus and leave to look for the student.
Assume the student has safely exited.
Walk to the back of the bus to see if the student got back on.
Ask another student if they have seen the student.

questions.correctAnswerText: Secure the bus and leave to look for the student.
questions.explanation: Secure the bus and check around and underneath it for the missing student.

questions.question: Where are the danger zones on a school bus?

options.text: In the front of the bus
To the sides of the bus
To the front, rear, and sides of the bus

questions.correctAnswerText: To the front, rear, and sides of the bus
questions.explanation: Danger zones are areas where children are most likely to be hit by the bus or another vehicle. These areas are in front, behind, and on both sides of the bus.

questions.question: What should a driver do before leaving the bus to check on waiting students?

options.text: Turn the bus off and take the key.
Ask a student to watch the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the bus off and take the key.
questions.explanation: Secure the bus by turning off the engine and taking the key. Then check around and under the bus for any missing student.

questions.question: When should mirrors be adjusted on a school bus?
questions.explanation: Check and adjust all mirrors before driving. This is critical for safe bus operation.
